```{r}
#| include: false
for (f in list.files("R", pattern = "\\.R$", full.names = TRUE)) source(f)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
clean_all <- nanoparquet::read_parquet("data/clean/outbreaks.parquet")
clean <- filter(clean_all, in_scope)
info <- freshness_info()
current <- current_season_info(info$as_of)
weekly <- weekly_counts(clean, current)
ranges <- bind_rows(baseline_range(weekly, "pre-pandemic", current),
                    baseline_range(weekly, "post-pandemic", current))
this_season <- filter(clean, season == current$season)
resp_this <- filter(this_season, outbreak_type == "Respiratory")
facilities_tbl <- readr::read_csv("data/clean/facilities.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
fmt_n <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
tbl <- function(x, ...) knitr::kable(x, format = "html", table.attr = 'class="table table-sm"', ...)
banner <- function() cat(freshness_banner_html(info))
```

### Row {height="30%"}

::: {.card title="Reading the chart"}

New outbreaks per week of onset, one per affected unit or ward, by setting.
Testing and reporting changed during the pandemic, so this season (blue) is
compared with **two separate ranges**: **pre-pandemic** (2016/17 to
2018/19, plus 2019/20 to early March 2020) and **post-pandemic** (2022/23
to 2025/26). The post-pandemic range is the fairer comparison; the
pre-pandemic one shows how far the baseline has moved. The last two weeks
are provisional.

:::

### Row {height="41%"}

```{r}
#| title: This season by week
weekly |>
  filter(season == current$season, setting == "All settings") |>
  select(week, type, n) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = n) |>
  left_join(ranges |> filter(setting == "All settings", type == "Respiratory", baseline == "post-pandemic") |>
              transmute(week, `Resp. post-pandemic range` = paste0(lo, "-", hi)), by = "week") |>
  arrange(desc(week)) |>
  transmute(`ISO week` = sprintf("W%02d", iso_week_of_season_week(week)), Respiratory,
            `Resp. post-pandemic range`, Enteric) |>
  tbl()
```

### Row {height="33%"}

::: {.card title="Reading the chart"}

Each outbreak is counted once; one where more than one pathogen was found
is shown as **Multiple agents**. *Unknown* means no agent was identified,
often because testing was not done or was negative, so it says as much
about testing as about the virus. Co-detections were recorded differently
before 2020 (one row, two agents) than after (separate rows). The table
counts an outbreak under every pathogen found.

:::

### Row {height="55%"}

```{r}
#| title: Respiratory outbreaks by pathogen and season
grp <- c("covid19", "influenza_a", "influenza_b", "rsv", "rhino_entero", "unknown")
clean |>
  filter(outbreak_type == "Respiratory") |>
  group_by(Season = season) |>
  summarise(Total = n(), across(all_of(paste0("agent_", grp)), sum)) |>
  rename_with(~ unname(AGENT_GROUPS[sub("^agent_", "", .x)]), starts_with("agent_")) |>
  arrange(desc(Season)) |>
  tbl()
```

### Row {height="45%"}

::: {.card title="Reading the alerts"}

Season start is flagged with the **moving epidemic method** (MEM), used by
ECDC and WHO Europe for influenza, applied to weekly outbreak counts with
the method's default settings and fitted on 2022/23 to 2025/26. The season
starts in the first complete week above the **epidemic threshold**; higher
lines mark medium, high and very high intensity. Counts are small, so a
single week just above the threshold can be noise: consecutive weeks above
it are the stronger signal. COVID-19 has no stable seasonal pattern yet, so
it is shown against the post-pandemic range without an alert
(latest complete week: `r utils::tail(covid_this$n, 1)` outbreaks).

:::

### Row {height="23%"}

```{r}
#| title: MEM thresholds (weekly outbreaks, all settings)
bind_rows(lapply(c("influenza", "rsv"), function(a) tibble(
  Agent = unname(ONSET_AGENTS[a]),
  Threshold = round(th[[a]]$epidemic, 1),
  Medium = round(th[[a]]$medium, 1), High = round(th[[a]]$high, 1),
  `Very high` = round(th[[a]]$very_high, 1),
  Started = if (st[[a]]$started) sprintf("W%02d", iso_week_of_season_week(st[[a]]$first_week)) else "No"
))) |>
  tbl()
```

### Row {height="33%"}

::: {.card title="Reading the curves"}

Time from onset until the outbreak was declared over, for outbreaks
beginning 2022/23 onward. Outbreaks still open count up to the data-as-of
date and are then **censored** (Kaplan–Meier), so recent outbreaks do not
make durations look shorter. Duration reflects the rules for declaring an
outbreak over (a set period with no new cases) as well as transmission.

:::

### Row {height="55%"}

```{r}
#| title: Median duration (days, Kaplan-Meier)
bind_rows(
  km_medians(resp_dur, "setting") |> mutate(Type = "Respiratory"),
  km_medians(filter(resp_dur, agent %in% names(agent_cols)) |> droplevels(), "agent") |>
    mutate(Type = "Respiratory"),
  km_medians(ent_dur, "setting") |> mutate(Type = "Enteric")
) |>
  transmute(Type, Group = group, Outbreaks = outbreaks, `Still open` = still_open,
            Median = median_days, `95% CI` = sprintf("%g-%g", ci_low, ci_high)) |>
  tbl()
```

# Facilities {orientation="columns"}

```{r}
#| include: false
fsc <- facility_season_counts(clean)
# Complete seasons only: 2015/16 starts in January 2016 and the current
# season is still in progress, so both would understate repeat outbreaks.
complete_seasons <- season_label(2016:(current$season_start_year - 1L))
rs <- repeat_share(fsc) |> filter(season %in% complete_seasons) |>
  mutate(setting = factor(setting, levels = names(SETTING_COLOURS)))
last_complete <- season_label(current$season_start_year - 1L)
dist <- recurrence_distribution(fsc) |> filter(season == last_complete) |>
  mutate(setting = factor(setting, levels = rev(names(SETTING_COLOURS))))
```

### Row {.tabset}

```{r}
#| title: Repeat outbreaks by season
girafe_dash(plot_repeat_share(rs), width = 9, height = 6.5)
```

```{r}
#| title: !expr paste("Episodes per facility,", last_complete)
girafe_dash(plot_recurrence_distribution(dist), width = 9, height = 5)
```

banner()

### Row {height="40%"}

::: {.card title="Reading the chart"}

A facility is a physical site (one address, split by setting where an LTCH
and a retirement home share it). The source records one outbreak per
affected ward, so wards affected together are grouped into one **episode**:
outbreaks of the same type at a facility each beginning within 14 days of
the previous one. A *repeat* is a later, separate episode in the same
season. Only facilities with at least one outbreak appear, and counts are
not adjusted for facility size, so facilities are deliberately not ranked.

:::

### Row {height="48%"}

```{r}
#| title: Facilities with repeat episodes
rs |>
  transmute(Season = season, Setting = setting, Facilities = facilities,
            `2+ episodes` = repeat_facilities, Share = sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * share_repeat)) |>
  arrange(desc(Season), Setting) |>
  tbl()
```

# About

## Row

::: {.card title="About this dashboard"}

An unofficial, independent surveillance summary built from the City of
Toronto's open dataset *Outbreaks in Toronto Healthcare Institutions*,
which Toronto Public Health refreshes every Thursday with data as of
Wednesday afternoon. It is updated automatically each week; the line at the
top right of every page shows how current the data are.

**What it counts.** Declared outbreaks in hospitals, long-term care homes
(LTCH) and retirement homes, by week of onset. The data contain no case
counts, attack rates or deaths, so everything here is outbreak-level.

**Main caveats.**
Outbreaks are recorded per unit or ward, not per facility.
Testing and reporting changed during the pandemic, so counts before and
after 2020 are not directly comparable.
Pathogen labels changed over the years and have been harmonized.
"Coronavirus" in the source means seasonal coronaviruses, not COVID-19.
Recent weeks are provisional because outbreaks are reported with a delay.
Counts reflect testing and reporting practices as well as disease activity.

**Sources and licence.** Contains information licensed under the
[Open Government Licence – Toronto](https://open.toronto.ca/open-data-license/):
*Outbreaks in Toronto Healthcare Institutions*, *Address Points (Municipal)*
and *Neighbourhoods*. Basemap © OpenStreetMap contributors © CARTO.
Not produced or endorsed by Toronto Public Health.

Methods and every analytical decision are documented in the
[project repository](https://github.com/samielsabri/toronto_healthcare_institutions_outbreaks),
including the [decisions log](https://github.com/samielsabri/toronto_healthcare_institutions_outbreaks/blob/main/reports/decisions.md).

:::
